transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2026-06-20 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 47 minutes
- Attendees: Alicia Chen, Marcus Patel (Redwood); Sara Nguyen, Tom Alvarez, Priya Shah, Rajesh Iyer, Evan Cole (HelioFinance)

Summary:
Quick preflight for vendor onboarding: legal wants DPA/MSA clarifications and exception path, FinOps wants committed spend bands and billing cadence, Security needs BYOK/KMS and audit log retention details. SE to run short performance pilot to prove latency/cost numbers for Dedicated pool sizing.

Topics covered:
- MSA redlines and DPA subprocessor list
- SLA targets (p99 latency), credits and remedies
- Pricing: hosted per-token vs dedicated committed bands, egress and KMS billing
- Pilot: 48h perf run, dataset and traffic profile
- Compliance artifacts: SOC2 report, pen test, subprocessor list, export controls

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alicia Chen: Hey everybody thanks for joining, we got about 45 minutes, i put an agenda in the invite, uh quick preflight to make sure legal and finops are aligned before we route to procurement.
[00:18] Sara Nguyen: Yep thanks Alicia, we're trying to get the onboarding clock started. main things: legal needs MSA/DPA clarity, finops needs committed spend numbers and how billing shows up, security has KMS/retention questions.
[00:35] Tom Alvarez: Hi all, from legal side we usually produce an exceptions matrix. for Redwood specifically we want to see the DPA subprocessor list and any escrow or data isolation options. also curious about the SLA credit calculation, how it's measured.
[00:54] Marcus Patel: Sure. quick framing: Redwood supports hosted, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC). SLA measurements are by per-route p99 latency and availability across region and model family. credits are tiered based on SLA breach windows; we can send the exact formula.
[01:18] Rajesh Iyer: when you say p99 measurement, where does the telemetry come from? is that customer-side probes or your control plane? we need audit logs and raw traces for compliance.
[01:31] Marcus Patel: Good question. telemetry is primarily from the serving runtime; we also offer tracing hooks and logs that can be streamed to a customer's S3 or kinesis. For Private deployments you control the control-plane access and logs; for Dedicated we can ship log exports and a token-level cost breakdown.
[01:54] Priya Shah: Pricing: we run models for user-facing features, spikes daily. we need committed spend to get Dedicated rates. can you explain the billing cadence and any egress, KMS charges?
[02:10] Alicia Chen: On billing, hosted is straight token pricing plus optional embedding charges, Dedicated is committed monthly capacity with overage rates. KMS BYOK is an add-on — if you bring your own key there is an extra per-month key-handling fee and sometimes per-request crypto cost for HSM-backed operations. egress usually follows cloud provider egress rules; we can model a path for you.
[02:35] Sara Nguyen: And is KMS encrypted at rest by default? we need to show this to audit.
[02:41] Marcus Patel: Yes data at rest is encrypted; for private customers you can integrate with your KMS (AWS KMS/GCP CMEK) or use Redwood-managed keys. We have SOC2 documentation and pen test summary we can share.
[02:58] Tom Alvarez: On the MSA, our counsel flagged the indemnity and data processing clauses. specifically — subprocessors, data retention, and deletion certs. is there an automated deletion confirmation?
[03:12] Alicia Chen: We can provide deletion attestations for the private + dedicated offerings; hosted customers can request deletion and we provide an audit event confirming deletion, but we should align on timelines in the DPA.
[03:25] Evan Cole: procurement here — timeline wise we need to know target signoff date and any upfront commit. what are typical procurement asks for enterprise?
[03:34] Alicia Chen: Typical path is: get MSA redline, sign committed spend for Dedicated if you want predictable throughput, spin up a pilot on hosted or a small Dedicated pool, run perf tests, then finalize SLA and billing. We can do monthly or annual billing.
[03:51] Priya Shah: for committed spend, what's the minimum? we want to model versus hosted.
[03:56] Marcus Patel: There's no one-size fits all — example commitments start around mid-five-figures monthly for Dedicated pools; that gets you predictable qps and lower per-token unit cost. We'll put your traffic profile into a sizing table.
[04:15] Sara Nguyen: ok let's get that sizing table. i'll share our token volume and peak qps.
[04:21] Marcus Patel: Great. for the pilot we'll need a traffic replay or synthetic profile. 48h run should show warm KV cache behavior and steady-state latency.
[04:33] Tom Alvarez: Regarding DPA subprocessor list — can you give us the list now or do you need procurement to sign something first?
[04:41] Alicia Chen: We can share the current subprocessor registry now; it includes our cloud infra providers and a couple third-party monitoring libraries. We'll attach it to the redline package.
[04:52] Rajesh Iyer: about BYOK — will using customer-managed KMS change latency or pricing?
[04:59] Marcus Patel: Minimal latency impact unless you're doing HSM-backed per-token crypto; typically key unwrap operations happen at session init. There might be marginal per-request crypt ops for HSM. We'll call that out in the security doc.
[05:14] Sara Nguyen: One more legal question — export controls and residency, we have eu customers so data residency matters. can Redwood guarantee EU-only processing?
[05:25] Alicia Chen: We have region routing and EU-hosted regions. For strict residency we recommend Private or Dedicated pinned to eu-region capacity; we'll put language in the DPA for residency obligations.
[05:37] Evan Cole: procurement — what about escrow or business continuity guarantees?
[05:42] Alicia Chen: For enterprise customers we offer an escrow pathway and runbooks; baked into certain enterprise contracts with an ops handover plan. I'll include that in the MSA appendix.
[05:53] Tom Alvarez: Great. on the SLA credits formula, could you give concrete examples for our procurement template?
[05:59] Marcus Patel: Example: p99 latency target 300ms for a given model family; if you hit 300-500ms, you get 10% credit; 500-1s 25% credit; >1s more escalated remediation. it's normally measured across the route and aggregated daily with a rolling 30-day window. we'll send the exact table.
[06:20] Priya Shah: For billing, do data egress and KMS costs get passed through or are they part of the bundle?
[06:26] Alicia Chen: Egress is typically passed through (cloud network egress). KMS add-on is a managed fee. For Dedicated committed contracts we can absorb some egress as part of the commitment — depends on the commit band.
[06:40] Sara Nguyen: ok. can you confirm if audit logs retention is 13 months by default? our policy wants 12 months plus archived for 7 years.
[06:49] Marcus Patel: Default is 12 months; we can extend retention for enterprise customers and export to your own S3/GCS for long-term archiving.
[06:59] Tom Alvarez: on data deletion certs — timeline?
[07:04] Alicia Chen: Standard deletion cert within 30 days, with a special clause available for shorter confirm windows in enterprise DPA.
[07:12] Evan Cole: i just want to flag that FinOps will want a runway for committed spend. what are cancellation or ramp-down terms?
[07:19] Alicia Chen: We typically have a minimum term for committed bands (monthly/annual). Ramp-downs incur a notice period; we'll include a pro-rated adjustment window in the contract.
[07:30] Priya Shah: could the pilot be billed to a short-term hosted invoice so we can validate cost before committing?
[07:36] Marcus Patel: Yes. Pilot can run on hosted pricing and then we model what Dedicated would have cost for the same volume. that helps show savings.
[07:46] Sara Nguyen: ok action wise: Alicia send MSA/DPA + security docs; Marcus run 48h pilot; we'll share traffic profile. Tom will give legal exceptions.
[07:55] Tom Alvarez: quick procedural — if we redline contract, do you accept counter-redlines or is that passed to legal? what's turnaround?
[08:03] Alicia Chen: We handle counter-redlines, usually 3-5 business days for initial review; for complex exceptions it'll go to our legal ops and could take longer. We'll flag priority items.
[08:12] Rajesh Iyer: one last note — we require a list of subprocessors and versioned SOC2 report with the last three pen test fixes.
[08:20] Marcus Patel: We'll include SOC2 and the pen test summary (redacted) and a current subprocessor registry.
[08:28] Sara Nguyen: timeline — if we get docs by Tuesday, legal reviews week of 29th, procurement targets first week of July.
[08:36] Alicia Chen: Sounds good. we'll aim to get the redline bundle by 6/23.
[08:41] Evan Cole: final — can you also provide a sample invoice layout so accounting can validate fields?
[08:47] Alicia Chen: Yes, will include sample invoice and billing cadence options.
[08:51] Marcus Patel: I'll start the perf pilot tonight, we'll use a synthetic replay and share a spreadsheet with latency distribution and token costs.
[08:59] Tom Alvarez: thanks everyone.
[09:01] Alicia Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up with next steps and action items in the thread.

End of transcript.
